analysis.title: USA: Warsh Does Not Address October FOMC Meeting but Says "World Has Broadly Conformed to Our Expectations" Since Last Meeting
key_insights: Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh did not address the October FOMC meeting at the IMF annual meetings. He said that "in the intermeeting period, the world has broadly conformed to our expectations" from the September meeting.

Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman said "I don't feel any urgency for taking further action at this point." San Francisco Fed President Daly, speaking after the firmer than expected September CPI report, said she did not see an urgent need "to decide with a limited set of information."
Goldman reads the Warsh, Bowman and Daly comments together as a sign that the FOMC will pause in October. Goldman continues to expect a second and final hike in December.
Warsh said the US is experiencing "a massive investment surge" tied to the AI buildout. He also noted a "synchronous tightening in monetary policy around the world" recently.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Goldman expects no rate move at the October meeting, based on Warsh, Bowman and Daly comments.

macro_indicators.reading: Second and final hike expected in December
macro_indicators.interpretation: Goldman's baseline is one more hike, in December, after which the tightening ends.
The report called the September CPI firmer than expected, but Daly still saw no urgent need to act on limited information.

risk_factors: A firmer inflation print such as the September CPI could change the pause call, although Daly and Bowman showed no urgency to act.

theme_stances.key_argument: Comments from Warsh, Bowman and Daly indicate the FOMC is set to pause in October, with a second and final hike still expected in December.
theme_stances.evidence: the FOMC is set to pause in October
